title: Week-2-DFS-Complete-Dossier
universal_lens: The dossier formalizes a constrained optimization over a high-dimensional, partially observed state space. It unifies discrete provenance tagging with continuous percentile metrics, mapping second-party salary proxies and mechanical projection bounds into a unified value-density operator subject to strict epistemic uncertainty.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the `[2P]` and `[FLAG]` tags as hierarchical Bayesian priors on parameter reliability. The `mean qualifying-pool percentile - salary percentile` acts as a conformal score, quantifying the deviation of an asset's role from its market pricing under incomplete lobby verification.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the mechanical floor/ceiling multipliers (0.55, 1.6) as bounded state-transition kernels for player output. Blowout-risk tier gaps function as dynamic environmental constraints that collapse the expected pass-volume manifold, forcing situational fade operators on underdog QBs.

primitives.name: Role-vs-Salary Value Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Formulas used in this dossier:** - *Role-vs-salary value score* (WR/TE pool): mean qualifying-pool percentile - salary percentile within the salaried pool.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Mean qualifying-pool percentile: dimensionless rank ratio [0, 1]; Salary percentile: dimensionless rank ratio [0, 1].
primitives.assumptions: Assumes percentiles are drawn from well-defined, stationary distributions; assumes linear additivity between role quality and inverse cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when the qualifying pool size approaches zero or when salary distribution exhibits extreme non-convex clustering, rendering percentile ranks unstable.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a Sharpe-like excess return metric in quantitative finance, measuring the gradient of performance relative to capital allocation.
layer2.telemetry: Observed via public OWS/DKN ownership figures and realized DFS point totals.

primitives.name: Optimizer Floor/Ceiling Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - *Optimizer floor/ceiling*: floor = 0.55 × projection; ceiling = 1.6 × projection (mechanical, not model-derived).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Floor: Expected fantasy points (lower bound); Ceiling: Expected fantasy points (upper bound); Projection: Base expected fantasy points.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes symmetric multiplicative volatility around a central deterministic projection; ignores contextual game-script modifiers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails catastrophically for binary outcome assets (e.g., kickers or backup RBs) where the underlying distribution is highly skewed rather than log-normal.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE bounded confidence intervals, providing a rigid geometric envelope for Monte Carlo lineup generation.
layer2.telemetry: Verified against Week 1 actual scoring distributions and subsequent roster lock outcomes.

primitives.name: Second-Party Provenance Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: The DK endpoint was Akamai-blocked on 2026-09-19, so **no salary in this dossier is lobby-verified**.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Akamai-blocked: Boolean network status; Lobby-verified: Binary truth value regarding official sportsbook data.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes all second-party sources share a correlated systematic bias if primary ground-truth endpoints are inaccessible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the secondary proxy sources diverge significantly from each other without a consensus resolution mechanism.

layer2.mapping: Functions as a GSI prior weight adjustment, heavily penalizing the information entropy of any optimization relying on `[2P]` inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Measured by the variance between `[2P]` salaries and eventual lobby-lock salaries.

The mathematical architecture of the dossier relies on constructing a robust optimization surface despite severe observational occlusion. By defining the Role-vs-Salary Value Operator, we establish a gradient vector field pointing toward maximum expected utility per unit of budget constraint. However, because the underlying salary manifold is entirely composed of second-party (`[2P]`) proxies due to Akamai blocking, the entire optimization problem is elevated into a probabilistic belief space. The Mechanical Projection Bounds act as a rigid, non-stochastic truncation of the tail risks, artificially stabilizing the variance of the portfolio. This creates a dual-layer system: a geometric core defined by fixed multipliers (0.55, 1.6) and a fuzzy outer shell governed by Bayesian provenance tags (`[FLAG]`, `[ELITE]`). When integrating the blowout-risk tier gaps—derived from Kalshi futures—we introduce a dynamic, game-script-dependent collapse of the offensive volume manifold. The opposing agents (the DFS field) are modeled implicitly through the ownership percentiles. If the value operator identifies a high-gradient asset that also resides in a low-ownership percentile band, it represents a localized arbitrage opportunity. The failure mode of this system occurs when the `[2P]` salary proxies exhibit a structural drift from the true lobby salaries, causing the value operator to misalign with the actual budget constraint at lock time.
